references.text: The story of Judah and Tamar in Gen 38:6-11 is the background for the Sadducees' question. Here Er, Judah's firstborn, dies without children, and his brothers are to raise up offspring for him in turn – the same pattern described in Luke 20:29.

Levirate marriage is commanded in Deut 25:5-6, where a brother must take his deceased brother's wife and raise up offspring for him. It is this law that the Sadducees refer to in their example with the seven brothers.

In Ruth 1:11-12, Naomi refers to levirate marriage when she explains that she has no more sons who can become husbands for her daughters-in-law – a parallel to the theme of successive marriages after a brother's death.
The parallel account in Matt 22:25-26 recounts the same example with seven brothers, where the first took a wife and died, and the second took her.
The parallel account in Mark 12:20-21 recounts the same example where seven brothers in turn married the same woman and died childless.
